title: bcrypt wall cost at BCRYPT_ROUNDS=12 on the production CPU
bead_closes: open question Q-6 (F-29's 902 us figure is void)

cost_factor.note: src/.env declares NO BCRYPT_ROUNDS key, so the live value is the CryptSettings class default. The live value and the default COINCIDE at 12, and that coincidence is RECORDED here rather than assumed: conflating 'the configured default' with 'the deployed value' is exactly what produced the void 902 us figure.

machine.match_evidence: cpu_model and core_count match the certified reports/app_host_report.json used for Phase 0 Step 4

protocol.definition_of_best_of: min-of-all-iterations for the floor, median-of-rep-medians for the central estimate
protocol.harness: /home/ansible/l15_bcrypt_cost.py (outside the repo: it is a harness, not app code)

bcrypt_gensalt.reading: negligible: ~2 us against a 271 ms hash. The cost is the key schedule, not the salt.

app_get_password_hash.what: src.app.core.security.password.get_password_hash - the app's async path, including ThreadPoolExecutor dispatch (BCRYPT_THREAD_POOL_SIZE=8)

verdicts.noise_floor_note: The programme declares +/-2x intra-arm and 7.1x run-to-run as noise; 1.09x is far inside it. The comment is NOT a benchmark and was NOT used as an input to this measurement - the finding is that it happens to be right, not that it was assumed.

f29_902us_void.note: THE BEAD PREDICTED ~2 ORDERS OF MAGNITUDE ABOVE THE DISCARDED FIGURE. The measured gap is ~300x, i.e. larger still. This is THE EXPECTED VALUE, NOT A REGRESSION, and must not be 'fixed'. The 902 us figure is incompatible with BCRYPT_ROUNDS=12 on any platform; bcrypt is a C extension and the OWASP floor is arithmetic, not environmental.

verdicts.executor_note: app path 273.193 ms vs raw hashpw 271.395 ms = +1.8 ms (~0.7%), inside the arm's own spread. The ThreadPoolExecutor costs nothing measurable at this work factor; recorded so the executor is not later 'optimised' on a false premise.

measured: bcrypt.hashpw costs 271.395 ms (median-of-rep-medians) at rounds=12 on i7-8850H / 4 cores
the app's async get_password_hash path costs 273.193 ms for the same work
bcrypt.gensalt contributes ~0.002 ms, i.e. negligible against the hash
the cost factor in force is 12, read from live settings, and src/.env declares no override

inferred_not_measured.claim: bcrypt is the dominant term in POST /account/login latency at 100 concurrency
inferred_not_measured.status: INFERRED from queueing arithmetic on two separately measured numbers - this is NOT an endpoint measurement
inferred_not_measured.arithmetic: 100 users x 271 ms = 27.1 CPU-seconds of hashing on 4 cores, i.e. ~6.8 s of wall time to drain a burst, against a pool of 8 bcrypt threads on 4 cores
inferred_not_measured.cross_reference: Phase 0 Step 4 baseline run 20261016_151856 measured POST /account/login (setup) median 3100 ms cold / 1000 ms warm at 100 users
inferred_not_measured.reading: the observed 1-3.1 s medians are the right order of magnitude for a saturated hashing pool, but attributing login latency to bcrypt requires a request-level profile, not this microbenchmark. Lane E item M-6 (FastAPI_saas-85l8) is the item that would settle it.

deviations_recorded_in_that_run: IP whitelist of the load host 192.168.121.142 (bypasses the IP-keyed admission counters only; the user-keyed tier policy still applied). Removed after the run.

closed.q6: F-29's 902 us bcrypt figure is void - 271.4 ms measured at rounds=12, ~301x above it
closed.consistency_with_config_comment: the '12=250ms' comment is consistent with the measurement to within 1.09x
